# Foundations of Game Theory
::: {.lead}
The formal core of game theory and the canonical games, worked through in R. Everything else on the site builds on it.
:::
:::

## What you'll be able to do by the end

- Model a strategic situation as a game and find its pure and mixed Nash equilibria.
- Recognise the canonical games (Prisoner's Dilemma, Hawk-Dove, coordination, bargaining, oligopoly) in new settings.
- Compare expected-utility, prospect-theory and ambiguity-averse decisions under uncertainty.
- Simulate replicator dynamics and identify evolutionarily stable strategies.
- Compute the Shapley value, the core and the nucleolus of a cooperative game.
- Contrast equilibrium predictions with bounded-rationality models such as QRE and level-k.
- Analyse strategic network formation, and place the field's results in their history.

## Who should take this course

Start here if game theory is new to you. The course assumes basic R (reading data, writing a function, drawing a ggplot2 plot) and school-level algebra.
